title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Gnarly Wipeout: Nvidia Sinks 14%, Nasdaq Drops 5.3%
conditions.summary: An AI and chip selloff turned into a rout, with Nvidia down 14% on a reported SEC accounting probe. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and joined the Dow in correction territory, while the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gain.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910, its seventh straight loss, and joined the Dow in correction territory.
The Nasdaq Composite sank 5.3% to 22,618, wiping out its gain for 2026; the Dow lost 1.9% to 48,147 and the Russell 2000 fell 2.8%.
Stocks opened only modestly lower, then the selling built all day as chip and AI names were dumped.
A Reuters report that SEC staff are examining Nvidia's accounting added to doubts about AI spending and Fed rate-hike worries.
For the week, the Nasdaq fell about 10%, the S&P 500 8.6% and the Dow 8%.
Semiconductors were the worst group by far; decliners swamped advancers.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: University of Michigan sentiment rose to 51.5 from 48.0, and one-year inflation expectations eased to 3.7% from 4.7%.
Fed Governor Lisa Cook said waiting too long to raise rates risks falling behind the curve; she had favored a hike in October.
Futures point to a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December being very likely.
Treasuries rallied as investors hunted for safety, pulling the 10-year yield to about 4.91%.
The VIX fear gauge jumped about 26% to near 36; gold fell 4.5% to about $3,518 and bitcoin slid below $59,000, while WTI crude rose about 1.6% to $83.73.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: NVDA (Nvidia): -14% — reported SEC accounting probe on top of the AI selloff; its worst day since the DeepSeek shock.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -13% — swept up in the chip rout.
AVGO (Broadcom): -12% — chip selling deepened into the close.
ANT (Anthropic): about -9% — the new IPO gave back more of its debut pop, closing near $89.
INTU (Intuit): about -9% or more — revenue outlook cut and slower Credit Karma growth outweighed a quarterly beat.
TSLA (Tesla): -7.6% and META (Meta Platforms): -5.9% — megacaps dragged down with tech.
ZS (Zscaler): up about 20% — report that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire it.
GAP (Gap): up about 12% midday — profit beat even as it trimmed its full-year sales outlook.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: BJ's Wholesale reported before the open: comparable club sales up 13.5% and a raised profit outlook, yet the stock slipped about 3% midday.
Gap reported after Thursday's close and rallied about 12% by midday on its profit beat.
Intuit reported after Thursday's close and slumped on its revenue outlook; it also agreed to sell Mailchimp for about $3.7 billion.
No major companies reported after Friday's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic completed its IPO at $83 a share, raising about $93.5 billion gross, plus a $26 billion private placement from big tech and chip partners.
Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia; the SEC declined to comment.
Asian chip stocks crashed overnight, with Taiwan's market suffering its steepest weekly drop since 1997.
Take-Two said GTA VI racked up about $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales.
BILL traded below the cash price in its agreed takeover by TPG and Corpay.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Weekend break; next session Monday, Nov 23, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom reporting after the close.
Tuesday: November consumer confidence; Best Buy, Dick's, Dollar Tree, Medtronic and Analog Devices before the open, Dell, Workday and Autodesk after.
Wednesday morning: Q3 GDP revision, October PCE inflation and durable goods, then the Fed's Beige Book; Deere reports.
Thursday: markets closed for Thanksgiving; Friday: stocks close early at noon Central.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November twentieth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water, and folks, that last set of the week was gnarly. Gus the wonder dog spent the whole afternoon hiding under the cabana deck from these waves. Come on out and say good evening, Gus! Okay, here's the final set. The S and P five hundred fell three point seven percent to about six thousand nine hundred ten. That's seven losses in a row, and it puts the index in correction territory, right next to the Dow. The Nasdaq got hit hardest, down five point three percent to about twenty-two thousand six hundred eighteen. That wipes out its whole gain for the year. The Dow dropped one point nine percent, and the Russell two thousand lost almost three percent. For the week, the Nasdaq is down about ten percent. That's a wipeout. The morning started calm, but the selling built all day in chips and A I stocks. The big riptide was Nvidia. A Reuters report said S E C staff are looking at its accounting, and the stock plunged fourteen percent. The old Kahuna of the A I trade had its worst day since the DeepSeek scare. A M D fell thirteen percent, and Broadcom dropped twelve. Anthropic, the grommet of the lineup after this week's giant I P O, slid about nine percent to near eighty-nine dollars. Intuit sank about nine percent on a softer revenue outlook. Now the wind and weather. The fear gauge, the VIX, jumped to nearly thirty-six. Investors ran to Treasuries, and the ten-year yield fell to about four point nine one percent. Gold dropped four and a half percent, and bitcoin slipped below fifty-nine thousand dollars. Crude oil bucked the tide, up about one and a half percent. On the data side, consumer sentiment from the University of Michigan rose to fifty-one point five, and inflation expectations cooled. But Fed Governor Lisa Cook said waiting too long to raise rates risks falling behind the curve. Markets see a December rate hike as very likely. Not every board went under, though. Zscaler jumped about twenty percent on a report that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy it. Zscaler caught the one clean wave of the day and rode it to the beach. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Gap also hung ten, up about twelve percent midday after a profit beat. In beach talk, Anthropic closed its I P O, raising about ninety-three billion dollars. And Take-Two said Grand Theft Auto six sold almost three point eight billion dollars on day one. Tomorrow's forecast: it's the weekend, so we wax the boards. Monday, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom report after the close. Tuesday brings consumer confidence plus Best Buy, Dell and Workday. Wednesday morning has G D P, P C E inflation and durable goods. Thursday the market is closed for Thanksgiving, and Friday closes early at noon Central. Soul surfers, days like this test your stance, so stay steady. Want a read on a ride? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. And catch the Dawn Patrol Monday morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
